In JavaScript, "truthy" and "falsy" refer to how values are evaluated in a Boolean context, such as in if statements or logical operations.
Falsy Values:
Falsy values are those that evaluate to false when converted to a Boolean. There is a specific, limited set of falsy values in JavaScript:
false (the boolean primitive)
0 (the number zero)
-0 (negative zero)
0n (BigInt zero)
"" (an empty string)
null
undefined
NaN (Not-a-Number)
Truthy Values:
Truthy values are all values that are not falsy. This means they evaluate to true when converted to a Boolean. Examples of truthy values include:
true (the boolean primitive)
Any non-zero number (e.g., 1, -1, 42, 3.14)
Any non-empty string (e.g., "hello", "false", " ")
Objects (including empty objects {} and empty arrays [])
Functions
Symbols
